We have target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We need propose retrosynthesis route using templates 1914393, then 1914394, then 1914395 in this order. So first apply template 1914393 to target to get precursors (first disconnection). Then apply 1914394 to one of the precursors (probably the aromatic side chain) to get further precursors. Then apply 1914395 to a precursor (maybe the fluorinated azetidine? Actually template 1914395 seems to convert a fluorine attached to a carbon in a heterocycle to an OH (or reverse). The retro template is O-CH... -> F-CH... So in retrosynthesis, applying template 1914395 will replace a fluorine with OH (i.e., break C-F bond to give an alcohol). In our target, we have a N4CC(F)C4 (a fluorinated azetidine). So retro step would replace that fluorine with OH, giving a hydroxy azetidine precursor.

Thus route: target -> apply 1914393 gives two fragments: one is aromatic ring with Cl-CH2? Actually template 1914393 appears to be a disconnection of a C-N bond linking an aniline to a heterocycle? Let's examine retro_smarts_template: '[#7:7]-[C:6]-[c:5]1:[c:4]:[c:3]:[c:2](-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[n;H0;D3;+0:12]2:[#7;a:11]:[#7;a:10]:[c:14]:[c:13]:2):[c:9]:[c:8]:1>>Cl-[CH2;D2;+0:1]-[c:2]1:[c:3]:[c:4]:[c:5](-[C:6]-[#7:7]):[c:8]:[c:9]:1.[#7;a:10]1:[#7;a:11]:[nH;D2;+0:12]:[c:13]:[c:14]:1'

So retro: product (left side) is an anilide attached to heterocycle; precursors are a chloromethyl aryl (Cl-CH2-aryl) and a heterocycle with NH. So applying to target will give two fragments: a chloromethyl phenyl (maybe the phenyl bearing the OMe) and a heterocycle fragment (the triazine? Actually c2nnn... is a 1,2,4-triazine? The heterocycle with N's). So we will get fragment1: Cl-CH2-aryl (the aryl is the anisole ring). Fragment2: heterocycle with NH (maybe the triazine with amine). Let's apply using tool apply_template to get precursors.
